text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The caretaker federal cabinet has reverted to a six-day working week, stopped new development schemes, cancelled licences of liquefied petroleum gas given on political basis, stopped the sale of Burmah Castrol shares in the state-run Pakistan Petroluem Ltd, banned new recruitment and closed the prime minister's monitoring and evaluation cell.
- Khawaja Tariq Rahim was sworn in as Governor Punjab province and Muhammad Arif Bangash as Governor of the North Western Frontier Province.
- Dissolved National Assembly (lower house) speaker Yousaf Raza Gilani has challenged the dissolution order of the President in the Supreme Court.

- The Deputy Inspector General of Police, Karachi range, Shoaib Suddle, accused of involvement in the murder of Murtaza Bhutto, brother of ex-prime minister Benazir Bhutto, was granted pre-arrest bail by the Sindh High Court.
- Ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto said the president had acted against her because he felt under threat from an anti-corruption bill she had moved in the parliament.

- An earthquake measuring 4.3 on the Richter scale and lasting almost six minutes hit the sparsely populated mountain region of central Balochistan. Tremors were also felt in Karachi, some 370 km (210 miles) southeast of the epicentre.
- Pakistani exports dropped by 2.9 percent in October compared to September in spite of repeated devaluation of rupee.
- A run on development financial institutions subsided after a huge withdrawal of 255 million rupees within two days.
- A trade delegation from Pakistan arrived in Baghdad looking for contracts to export food and medicine after the United Nations eased sanctions on Iraq.
- The rate of inflation increased in October to 11.03 percent year on year.
- A 78-member delegation of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry will meet caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid on Tuesday.
- The caretaker government has decided to continue the policy of the previous government regarding foreign investment in public sector enterprises.
